{{Quote|My mother was a captain in the Grand Army of the Republic. She died in the battle of T'olan, in the Wuun system&hellip;''"<br />"''I know it. That was a terrible battle.|Trever Flume and Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="TDM" />}}
The '''Battle of T'olan''' took place early in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], sometime around [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], when the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] fought at [[T'olan]], a location in the [[Wuun system]]. During the fierce conflict, a [[Captain/Legends|captain]] in the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]], the [[Trever Flume's mother|mother]] of a [[Gender/Legends|boy]] named [[Trever Flume]], was [[Death/Legends|killed]].

==Prelude==
The [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] began in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] when a number of [[Planet/Legends|worlds]], allied as the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], seceded from the dominant [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] government, the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

In order to fight with the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]], a [[Trever Flume's mother|woman]] left [[Gender/Legends|her]] family on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Bellassa/Legends|Bellassa]]. Just before she departed, she told her son, [[Trever Flume]], that he could not join her in the fight and promised to return to him safely.<ref name="TDM" />

==The battle==
Early in the war, the Republic fought at a location known as [[T'olan]] in the [[Wuun system]]<ref name="TDM" /> of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="TEAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Wuun system|T'olan system]]</ref> The battle was [[Blood/Legends|bloody]], and Trever Flume's mother [[Death/Legends|died]] there, fighting as a [[Captain/Legends|captain]].<ref name="TDM" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|You're not going without me.''"<br />"''It's a two-person ship. There's no room. I'll be back&mdash;''"<br />"''No! Don't say that. Just&hellip; don't. I can help.|Trever Flume persuades [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Ferus Olin]] to take him to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] during the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]]|<ref name="Underworld">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Underworld]]''</ref>}}
The Clone Wars concluded with the [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] of the Republic's successor, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="TNEC" /> By [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]],<ref name="TERC on TDM">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' places ''[[The Last of the Jedi: The Desperate Mission]]'' in "c. [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]]."</ref> the Empire had subjugated the planet of Bellassa and killed [[Trever Flume's father]] and [[Tike Flume|brother]] in a bombing. Orphaned by this,<ref name="TDM" /> Trever Flume spiraled into an angry, confused depression<ref name="SW">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Secret Weapon]]''</ref> from which he emerged as a member of the Bellassan [[Black market/Legends|black market]], haunted by the deaths of each family member.<ref name="TDM" /> Because of what his mother had said before she left, and his father and brother saying much the same thing before their deaths, he became deeply nervous when people he cared about promised to return from danger without allowing him to come.<ref name="Underworld" />

[[Standard month/Legends|Months]] after being orphaned, Trevor Flume explained his situation to the former [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. [[Standard year/Legends|Years]] had passed since the battle of T'olan, yet Kenobi recalled its deadly reputation when Flume mentioned his mother's death.<ref name="TDM" />

==Behind the scenes==
The battle of T'olan was first mentioned in the young reader novel ''[[The Last of the Jedi: The Desperate Mission]]'' ([[2005]]) by author [[Jude Watson]]. The name of the battle was not capitalized in the novel.<ref name="TDM" />

In ''The Desperate Mission'', Trever Flume said that his mother had fought in the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]], but this could not have been the case.<ref name="TDM" /> ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' ([[2012]]) states that only [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] served in the Grand Army.<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Those [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] were all men<ref name="Warfare78">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' identifies the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] as an "[[Army/Legends|army]] of [[Cloning/Legends|identical]] [[Gender/Legends|men]]."</ref> and nigh<ref name="SBES">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]'' stars the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] [[X1]] and [[X2]], whose [[Falon Grey|genetic template]] was not [[Jango Fett]].</ref> exclusively sourced from the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]]. On the other hand, Jedi Generals and [[Jedi Commander/Legends|Jedi Commanders]] were considered part of the Grand Army and were not clones, but they significantly outranked the [[Clone Captain/Legends|captains]], who were clones. Nonetheless, there were non-clone branches of the Military fighting for the Republic, such as the [[Planetary Security Forces]] or the [[Judicial/Legends|Judicials]].<ref name="Warfare" />

Another [[Star Wars: The Last of the Jedi|''The Last of the Jedi'']] book, [[The Last of the Jedi: Death on Naboo|''Death on Naboo'']] ([[2006]]), said that the Galactic Empire had killed Trever Flume's mother while she was fighting against them,<ref name="DON">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Death on Naboo]]''</ref> but the Galactic Empire had not yet been founded when she died.<ref>''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places the [[Declaration of a New Order|founding]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], immediately before the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|end]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. According to ''[[The Last of the Jedi: The Desperate Mission]]'', [[Trever Flume's mother]] [[Death/Legends|died]] "early in the wars."</ref> Trever also remembered his mother dying on Bellassa, rather than at T'olan, in ''[[The Last of the Jedi: A Tangled Web]]'' (2006).<ref name="ATW">''[[The Last of the Jedi: A Tangled Web]]''</ref> These books conflated her with her partner and other son,<ref name="DON" /><ref name="ATW" /> whom ''The Desperate Mission'' established as having died at Imperial hands on Bellassa,<ref name="TDM" /> but ''A Tangled Web'' also explicitly mentioned the deaths of those two as independent of hers.<ref name="ATW" />
